Triage (R+89, triage seat, session `session_019kDRpB7D2XzVzkaLp57T5D`): **`pm:queue`** · **`priority:p1`** · `domain:engine` · type **Bug**.

p1: a stock showcase boot answers 500 on `GET /api/v1/packages`, which Studio calls three times on every open, and it has been reachable since #12348 (2026-08-25) — user-visible on the reference app, on `main` today.

**Cross-domain single PR, designated by the triage seat (the exception path):** the root cause and the defence sit in two lanes' packages, and splitting them would ship a registry that still serialises a live engine for one more round. The engine seat claims with the full file surface declared in the claim: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`installPackage` stores a spec-shaped manifest **projection** — id, name, version, namespace, type, scope, description, dependencies, declared metadata — and drops runtime-only members such as plugin instances; the kernel keeps the live object), `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (`registerApp` hand-off, if the projection lives there), **and** `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` (`GET /packages` / `GET /packages/:id` project explicit fields instead of spreading the item — a future non-serialisable member degrades to a missing field, never a 500). Pins per the card: a registry test with a reference-cycle-carrying manifest asserting `JSON.stringify(registry.getPackage(id))` succeeds, plus a route test over the showcase-shaped stack. Not clause ②: the published response gains nothing and loses only fields that were never serialisable. Hot file: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the engine seat answers fold-or-serial against #14147 / #14205).

Pair: #14310 (the missing 5xx log line, `domain:cli`) — the same dogfood, different defect; ⛔ not folded.

Size/model suggestion: M, `opus`.

Claim amendment (same session, `session_62849a16-0144-4728-8942-9f60bb3a73f1`, branch `claude/issue-14309-packages-serializable-manifest`) — one file added to the declared surface, with the measurement that forced it.

Added: `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (+ a new sibling test).

Why: the card attributes the list/detail 500 to `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts`. Measured on a live showcase boot, that is not the handler that answered. `GET /api/v1/packages/no.such.package` returns `Package 'no.such.package' not found` — the runtime domain's spelling; the REST twin says `Package "no.such.package" was not found.` And `GET /api/v1/packages/com.objectstack.setup` returns the installed-package record directly under `data`, which is `deps.success(pkg)` in the runtime domain; the REST twin wraps it as `data.package` with a `source` stamp.

The producer fix stays exactly where the claim put it (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) and fixes all four routes on its own. What the added file carries is the route-level defence the triage designated — applying it only to the REST twin would ship a defence with a hole precisely where the defect was observed, so it is applied at both twins. Same defect class, same gate families, no new contract surface; `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` stays in scope and is edited as designated. No open PR touches any of the three files (checked across the 15 open PRs).

Surface now: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts`, their tests, and `.changeset/`.

PM decisions on the two open questions in the os-dev report (PM discretion — neither touches product semantics or a public contract):

1. **Hand-listed projection fields at the two package doors — keep A (what shipped).** Publishing a newly declared record field stays an explicit decision at each door, and drift surfaces as a missing field, never a 500. B (deriving the key set from `packages/spec`) would make the published surface a side effect of a schema edit and add a spec import edge to `packages/rest`; no measured pull for it.
2. **#14504 (packages/runtime type-checks none of its test files) — A: land this PR now, dispatch #14504 separately.** The new pin was type-checked standalone (exit 0); onboarding 208 pre-existing test files to `check:test-typecheck` is unrelated repair and does not ride a P1 fix.

Review of PR #14499 continues once its checks settle; findings #14503 and #14504 stay unassigned for triage.

1. **Acceptance evidence on the merged tree (`origin/main` @ `159e05e8` + its narrower fix), real showcase boot** — all four doors 200 (`GET /api/v1/packages` 26 rows, `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.showcase`, `GET /api/v1/meta/package` 26 rows, `POST /api/v1/packages/com.example.showcase/duplicate`), zero `Converting circular structure` lines in the server log, and the duplicate's `sys_packages` persist verified **directly** by reading the sqlite file afterwards: 1 row, `com.acme.dupbase`, manifest 411,662 bytes — the `JSON.stringify` that used to throw now lands. That direct-read check is worth repeating on #14499's head, since its own live verification predates several main merges.
2. **One behaviour difference for the reviewer to accept deliberately, not as a side effect:** #14499 drops function-valued manifest members (`onEnable`) from the stored record by shape; the parked #14442 fix only removed instantiated kernel plugins from `plugins[]` (discriminator `typeof entry.init === 'function'`, the same predicate the CLI's `isHostConfig` uses) and left every other member byte-identical. #14499's broader structural rule is the right floor — a record holds only data, and it covers install paths `AppPlugin` never touches — but the `onEnable` drop is a real change that deserves an explicit yes.

The parked branch `claude/issue-14442-package-record-serializable` (head `c80b5c4c3`, 4-case pin `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.package-record-serializable.test.ts`) stays on the remote for reference and is **not** going to become a PR. Patch round (same claim, same branch) — PR #14499 was `mergeable=dirty`, so CI had run zero checks on it. Merged `origin/main` and resolved by intent; the PR now reads `mergeable=true`.

**Merge sha `6257819c3`** (merge commit) + **`6961d6ec9`** (regeneration commit, current head). Base was `13bf05d3f`.

**One real code conflict, and it was not a formatting one.** `main` landed #14375, which stamps an ADR-0070 D2 writability verdict on every `/packages` row (`withWritableVerdict`). It collided with this card's field projection in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`. Resolved as **project first, stamp second** — `withWritableVerdict(qlService, toPackageResponse(row))` — because the order is load-bearing in one direction only: `toPackageResponse` is an allowlist of the declared record fields and `writable` is not one of them, so stamping first would have let the projection delete #14375's field, silently, as a 200 with the field simply absent. `withWritableVerdict` reads only `manifest.id`, which the projection keeps, so it is indifferent to running second. Pinned so a future reorder is a red test rather than a missing field (`stamps the #14375 writable verdict AFTER the projection, on both doors`).

**The same collision, caught on the REST side by reading rather than by a red.** #14375 also has the protocol stamp `writable` on every item leaving `getMetaItems({type:'package'})`, with `packages/rest/src/package-list-writable-carry.test.ts` pinning that this door CARRIES it. The REST allowlist added by this card did not list `writable` and would have dropped it. `writable` is now listed there explicitly, alongside `_diagnostics`, both annotated as producer-stamped values rather than record fields. ⚠️ This is exactly the hand-list drift hazard flagged in `open_questions` item 1 of the report above — it materialised within a day, which is worth weighing when that question is answered.

**Generated artifact: regenerated, not hand-merged.** `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` is `merge=os-regen`-routed. The merge commit was made by hand with `MERGE_HEAD` present, which is the hook's deferral path, then `pnpm gen:system-context-census` ran on the merged tree and the regeneration landed as its own commit — the hook confirmed `deferred regeneration discharged — all artifacts current, marker cleared`. 44 anchors were rewritten, mostly main's own drift. Measured rather than assumed that no other generated side was silently dropped: after the merge, of the 18 `merge=os-regen` path patterns, the only one where this head differs from `origin/main` is that census file, which this branch owns and which was then regenerated.

The two suites this merge could have broken were also run on their own, named rather than assumed covered: `packages-writable-verdict.test.ts` + `packages-serializable-response.test.ts` = 18 passed, and `package-list-writable-carry.test.ts` + `package-registry-item-projection.test.ts` = 10 passed.
